newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary rains damage wheat quality, good for maize.
newsitem.headline: Hungary rains damage wheat quality, good for maize.

text.p: Rain in Hungary is likely to result in the lowest quality wheat crop for many years, grains traders said on Friday.
"Most of the news on wheat harvesting is bad," Istvan Grebats of Termin brokerage told Reuters, adding that maize, on the other hand, would benefit from the moderate temperatures.
He said that the customary 60-40 milling wheat to feed wheat ratio in the harvest will be significantly different this year with a lot of low-quality wheat expected.
"I would say the ratio is likely to be 40 percent to 60 percent," Grebats said.
Another trader said early feedback on wheat quality were not encouraging.
"We have heard of very bad quality in some places, excellent quality elsewhere, but almost nothing in between," said Gyorgy Pilaszy of grains trading company Agrograin.
Grebats said that would leave farmers in highly different positions after the harvest.
"Some of them will be able to sell their (good quality) wheat like hot cakes, while others will have trouble just storing their wheat (of lower quality)".
He added that this year's wheat crop, while almost certain to reach the expected five million tonnes compared with last year's 3.9 million, was likely to be the lowest-quality crop in many years.
Pilaszy, however, said that earlier agriculture ministry forecasts of a five million tonne wheat crop were exaggerated.
"Four to 4.5 million tonnes would be a more realistic figure," he said, but added that it would be too early to estimate the proportion of milling and feed wheat within the total.
Rain was likely to hold throughout the weekend and with wheat harvesting already started in most parts of Hungary, except the northern regions, that was bad news, Pilaszy said.
"Now that the harvesting is on, every drop of rain is bad news".

But cold and rainy weather was almost ideal for maize and barring a drought during the next four weeks, the crop could even exceed last year's already good harvest of near six million tonnes, traders said.

According to agriculture ministry figures, frosts, flood and hailstorms have caused 9.5 billion forints worth of damage to the agriculture in the first half of the year and since the beginning of July another two billion worth of damage has been reported.
